title: David and Goliath
text:
The armies of Israel and the Philistines faced each other across the valley of Elah. Every morning and evening for forty days, a Philistine champion named Goliath came out and challenged Israel to send a man to fight him in single combat. He was a giant, armored in bronze from head to foot, with a spear whose shaft was like a weaver's beam. No Israelite dared face him.

David, a young shepherd, had come to the camp only to bring food to his older brothers. He heard the challenge and offered to fight. King Saul doubted him: he was just a boy. David replied that he had protected his father's sheep from lions and bears and killed them.

Saul dressed David in his own armor and gave him his sword. David took a few steps and took them off again. He was not used to them. Instead he went down to the stream, picked out five smooth stones, put them in his shepherd's bag, and walked out with his staff and his sling.

Goliath scorned the boy. David ran toward him, put a stone in the sling and let it fly. It struck the giant in the forehead and sank in, and Goliath fell face down. David ran over, took Goliath's own sword and killed him with it. When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.
lesson: Do not fight a stronger opponent on his terms or in borrowed armor. Use the skills you have actually practiced, at the distance where they work.
date: ancient Israelite tradition, set c. 1000 BC
caveat: Another verse, 2 Samuel 21:19, credits a man named Elhanan with killing Goliath, and scholars debate the history behind the story.
